headline: 11 policemen suspended over torture of Swechchhasebak Dal leader in Rangpur
summary: The officers were suspended following allegations of torture against a political leader in the Rangpur region.
details: Eleven police officers have been suspended from duty following allegations of torture involving a leader of the Swechchhasebak Dal in Rangpur.
The action was taken as part of an investigation into the conduct of the officers during the interrogation of the political leader.
The suspension serves as a measure to ensure a fair investigation into the claims of physical abuse and misconduct by the law enforcement agency.
Authorities have stated that any officer found guilty of violating human rights or official protocols will face strict disciplinary action.
caption:
11 police officers suspended in Rangpur.

Eleven police officers have been suspended from duty following allegations of torture involving a leader of the Swechchhasebak Dal in Rangpur.

The action was taken as part of an investigation into the conduct of the officers during the interrogation of the political leader.

The suspension serves as a measure to ensure a fair investigation into the claims of physical abuse and misconduct by the law enforcement agency.

Authorities have stated that any officer found guilty of violating human rights or official protocols will face strict disciplinary action.

headline_marked: Tk 40 for 70 metres: [[Dhaka rain turns short walks into costly rides]]
headline: Tk 40 for 70 metres: Dhaka rain turns short walks into costly rides
summary: Severe waterlogging after Friday's rain forced pedestrians to pay high fares to cross tiny stretches of road in areas like Garden Road and Green Road.
details: Heavy rain for two hours on Friday afternoon left several areas of Dhaka submerged, turning short walks into expensive commutes for office-goers and students.
On Garden Road behind Bashundhara City, rickshaw pullers charged Tk 40 to ferry passengers across a submerged stretch of only 70 metres.
A similar situation occurred on Green Road, where van drivers charged Tk 20 each to transport passengers from the University of Asia Pacific to Ananda Cinema Hall.
Drivers claimed the higher fares were justified because they had to wade through chest-deep water to steer their vehicles, making the work significantly harder.
Water entered several shops and homes in Eskaton Garden Road, Old Dhaka, Mirpur, and Moghbazar, forcing shopkeepers to move their goods to safer locations.
Commuters expressed frustration, stating they had no choice but to pay the extra costs to avoid ruining their clothes and shoes in the murky water.
The rain began after 3:00 pm and continued for two hours, catching many people without umbrellas as the morning had been hot and sunny.
